It is listed on BSE and NSE in India.{{Cite web |title=Business solutions {{!}} Tata Teleservices Maharashtra (TTML) |url=https://www.tatatelebusiness.com/aboutus-ttml/ |access-date=2023-11-02 |website=Tata Tele Business Services |language=en-IN}}{{Cite web |title=Tata Teleservices {{!}} Business {{!}} Tata group |url=https://www.tata.com/business/tata-teleservices |access-date=2023-11-02 |website=www.tata.com |language=en}}{{Cite web |title=TataTeleservice Share Price, TataTeleservice Stock Price, Tata Teleservices (Maharashtra) Ltd. Buy/Sell Tata Teleservices (Maharashtra) Ltd. news & tips, & F&O Quotes, NSE/BSE Forecast News and Live Quotes |url=https://www.moneycontrol.com/india/stockpricequote/telecommunications-service/tatateleservicesmaharashtra/TTM01 |access-date=2023-11-02 |website=www.moneycontrol.com |language=en |last1=Com |first1=Moneycontrol }} ==History== On 13 March 1995, Tata Tele (Maharashtra) Limited was founded as Hughes Ispat Limited, operating under the legal framework of the Companies Act of 1956. On 26 April 2000, the company changed its name to Hughes Tele.com (India) Limited to reflect its emphasis on broadband services.{{Cite web |title=Tata Teleservices (Maharashtra) > Company History > Telecommunications - Service > Company History of Tata Teleservices (Maharashtra) - BSE: 532371, NSE: TTML |url=https://www.moneycontrol.com/company-facts/tatateleservicesmaharashtra/history/TTM01 |access-date=2023-09-14 |website=www.moneycontrol.com |language=en |last1=Com |first1=Moneycontrol }} On 13 February 2003, the company underwent a name change to Tata Teleservices (Maharashtra) Limited. It currently operates as a subsidiary of Tata Teleservices Limited.{{Cite web |title=Company History of Tata Teleservices (Maharashtra) - BSE: 532371, NSE: TTML |url=https://www.sebi.gov.in/takeover/tatatele.pdf |access-date=2023-09-14 |website=www.sebi.gov.in |language=en}} In 2009, the company introduced mobile voice calling based on a pay per use model.{{cite web | title=Tata Tele to charge per call, no matter the duration | website=The Economic Times | date=2 September 2009 | url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/tata-tele-to-charge-per-call-no-matter-the-duration/articleshow/4964130.cms | access-date=14 September 2023}} According to [[Business Today (India)|Business Today]] Report, in November 2010, Tata Teleservices became the first private [[telecommunication]]s operator to launch 3G services in [[India]].{{cite web | title=Tata DoCoMo launches 3G services | website=Business Today | date=3 November 2010 | url=https://www.businesstoday.in/technology/news/story/tata-docomo-launches-3g-services-15326-2010-11-03 | access-date=14 September 2023}} Tata Teleservices operates a long fibre optic network spanning 132,000 kilometres and has a presence in over 70 cities. Tata Teleservices operates as a channel partner-based organization with a partner model encompassing approximately 1800+ partners nationwide.{{cite web | last=Abbas | first=Muntazir | title=Tata Teleservices, FirstWave to launch cybersecurity solutions | website=ETTelecom.com | date=18 August 2020 | url=https://telecom.economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/tata-teleservices-firstwave-to-launch-cybersecurity-solutions/77615793 | access-date=14 September 2023}} In February 2008, TTSL announced that it would provide [[CDMA]] mobile services targeted towards the youth, in association with the [[Virgin Group]] on a franchisee model basis. In November 2008, Japanese telecom giant [[NTT Docomo]] acquired{{how|date=February 2025}} a 26 per cent equity stake in Tata Indicom, a subsidiary of Tata Teleservices, for about {{INRConvert|130.7|b}} or an [[enterprise value]] of {{INRConvert|502.69|b}}.{{cite web|url=http://www.business-standard.com/india/storypage.php?tp=on&autono=49385 |title=NTT DoCoMo buys 26% in Tata Tele for $2.7 bn |publisher=Business-standard.com |access-date=2010-07-16}} [[NTT DoCoMo]] announced on 25 April 2014 that they would sell their shares in Tata Indicom to Tata Teleservices and exit the Indian market. The company had reported a loss of $780 million during financial year ending 31 March 2014.[http://in.reuters.com/article/uk-ntt-docomo-tata-teleserv-idINKBN0DB00X20140425 Docomo Exit]{{dead link|date=September 2024|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}} By 1 April 2015, all{{Clarify|reason=Wordwide? Across India? What was the deal here?|date=February 2025}} Virgin Mobile CDMA and [[GSM]] customers have been migrated into the umbrella Tata Indicom brand (Tata Indicom for Mumbai NCR). In April 2015 Tata Teleservices dropped the [[DoCoMo]] from its telecom brand. According to [[The Hindu]] reporting, the decision was made several months prior to the termination of the telecommunications company's contract with the Japanese operator [[NTT DoCoMo]], allowing them to continue using the brand until the agreement's conclusion.{{cite web |last=S |first=Rajalakshmi |date=25 April 2014 |title=NTT Docomo to exit Tata Teleservices |url=https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/companies/ntt-docomo-to-exit-tata-teleservices/article20760033.ece1 |access-date=14 September 2023 |website=BusinessLine}}{{cite web |last1=Dasgupta |first1=Pritha Mitra |last2=Kumar |first2=Arun |date=20 April 2015 |title=Tata Teleservices to drop DoCoMo from its telecom brand Tata Docomo |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/telecom/tata-teleservices-to-drop-docomo-from-its-telecom-brand-tata-docomo/articleshow/46981994.cms |access-date=14 September 2023 |website=The Economic Times}} In August 2017, Tata Teleservices sought to exit mobile network division due to large losses and debt, then sold its unit to [[Bharti Airtel]] in a debt free and cash-free deal and described as virtually free; [[Airtel]] will only pay a part of Tata Teleservices's unpaid spectrum payment liability.{{cite web |date=13 October 2017 |title=Tatas exit mobile biz, merge loss-making unit with Airtel |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/business/india-business/tatas-exit-mobile-biz-merge-loss-making-unit-with-airtel/articleshow/61060247.cms |access-date=13 October 2017 |work=Pankaj Doval and Reeba Zachariah |publisher=[[Times of India]]}}{{cite web |date=13 October 2017 |title=Tata Teleservices to sell its wireless mobile business to Bharti Airtel |url=http://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/company/corporate-trends/tata-teleservices-to-sell-its-wireless-mobile-business-to-bharti-airtel/articleshow/61051618.cms |access-date=13 October 2017 |work=Arijit Barman, Romit Guha |publisher=[[The Economic Times]]}}{{cite web |date=13 October 2017 |title=Bharti Airtel gets Tata Teleservices' mobile unit for nothing: All you need to know about the deal |url=http://www.firstpost.com/business/bharti-airtel-gets-tata-teleservices-mobile-unit-for-nothing-all-you-need-to-know-about-the-deal-4138127.html |access-date=13 October 2017 |publisher=Firstpost}} In November 2017, Tata Teleservices customers transitioned to the Airtel mobile network under an Intra Circle Roaming (ICR) arrangement. [[SIM card]]s and billing plans remained the same.{{cite web |date=22 November 2017 |title=Tata Teleservices mobile customers transition to Airtel |work=Airtel |url=https://www.airtel.in/press-release/11-2017/tata-teleservices-mobile-customers-start-transitioning-to-airtel-network |access-date=1 July 2019 |last1=Asthana |first1=Bhuvnesh }} The consumer mobile businesses of Tata Docomo, '''Tata Teleservices''' (TTSL) and Tata Teleservices Maharashtra Limited (TTML) have been merged into [[Bharti Airtel]] from 1 July 2019.{{cite web |date=1 July 2019 |title=Airtel Completes Merger of Tata |url=https://www.livemint.com/industry/telecom/airtel-completes-merger-of-tata-teleservices-consumer-mobile-business-1562001016569.html |access-date=4 July 2019 |publisher=Livemint}}{{cite web |date=1 July 2019 |title=Airtel's Tata merger deal |url=https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/info-tech/airtel-tata-tele-merger-completed/article28251509.ece |access-date=3 July 2019 |publisher=Business Line}}{{cite news |date=11 April 2019 |title=DoT approved deal of Tata and Bharti Airtel |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/telecom/telecom-news/tata-teleservices-merger-dot-seeks-rs-7200-crore-bank-guarantee-from-airtel/articleshow/68833052.cms |access-date=5 May 2019 |newspaper=Economic Times}} On 9 October 2017 Tata Teleservices announced it is preparing an exit plan for most of its 5,000-odd employees, which includes a notice of three to six months, severance packages for those willing to leave earlier, a voluntary retirement scheme (VRS) for elders, while transferring only a small part of its employees to other group companies.{{Cite news|url=http://economictimes.indiatimes.com/articleshow/60997241.cms|title=Tata Teleservices prepares exit plan for staff|last=Sengupta|first=Devina|date=2017-10-09|work=The Economic Times|access-date=2017-10-09}} On 12 October 2017, Bharti Airtel announced that it would acquire the consumer mobile businesses of Tata Teleservices Ltd (TTSL) and Tata Teleservices Maharastra Ltd (TTML) in a debt-free cash-free deal. The deal will essentially be free for Airtel which will only incur TTSL's unpaid spectrum payment liability. TTSL will continue to operate its enterprise, fixed line and broadband businesses and its stake in tower company Viom Networks.{{cite web|title=Bharti Airtel to acquire Tata's mobile business on debt-free cash-free basis|url=http://www.businesstoday.in/current/corporate/bharti-airtel-acquire-tata-teleservices-ttsl-consumer-mobile-business/story/261930.html|website=www.businesstoday.in|date=12 29 August 2018, Bharti Airtel, got its shareholders approval for the merger proposal with Tata Teleservices.{{cite news |title=Bharti Airtel shareholders approve merger proposal with Tata Teleservices extract: Tata Teleservices Limited along with its subsidiary Tata Teleservices (Maharashtra) Limited is an Indian internet services provider and IT services company headquartered in Mumbai, India.  It is listed on BSE and NSE in India.
